description:
The Establishment of Goat Unit (10 +1) scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This initiative is part of the broader strategy to promote animal husbandry and enhance the livelihood of rural households. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and technical support to small and marginal farmers. 

It specifically targets those who wish to establish goat farming units. 

Goat farming is recognized for its potential to provide a sustainable source of income. 

The scheme encourages the rearing of goats due to their adaptability to various climatic conditions. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to promote self-employment among rural youth. 

It aims to enhance the income of farmers through the establishment of goat units. 

The scheme sets a measurable target of establishing at least 10 goat units per beneficiary. 

Each goat unit consists of 10 female goats and 1 male goat. 

The total number of goats in each unit is therefore 11. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is substantial. 

Each beneficiary can receive up to ₹1.5 lakh for establishing a goat unit. 

This amount covers the cost of purchasing goats, housing, and other necessary infrastructure. 

The assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy. 

The subsidy rate is typically around 25% to 33% depending on the category of the beneficiary. 

For Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries, the subsidy can go up to 33%. 

For general category beneficiaries, the subsidy is 25%. 

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and aims to empower marginalized communities. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a small or marginal farmer. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old and not more than 55 years old. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at ₹1 lakh per annum for small farmers. 

For marginal farmers, the income limit is ₹50,000 per annum. 

Educational qualifications are not a strict requirement for this scheme. 

However, beneficiaries are encouraged to undergo training in goat rearing. 

The application process for the Establishment of Goat Unit (10 +1) is straightforward. 

Interested beneficiaries must approach the local Animal Husbandry Department. 

They need to fill out an application form that is available at the department office. 

Along with the application, beneficiaries must submit certain documents. 

These documents typically include proof of identity, proof of land ownership, and income certificate. 

A project report detailing the proposed goat unit may also be required. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the department officials. 

If approved, beneficiaries are informed about the subsidy amount and the next steps. 

The disbursement of funds is usually made in installments. 

The first installment is released upon the approval of the project. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the goat unit establishment. 

The timeline for fund disbursement can vary but is generally completed within six months. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

This department operates under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

Each state has its own Animal Husbandry Department to facilitate the scheme. 

Beneficiaries can contact their respective state departments for more information. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is also anticipated to improve the nutritional status of rural households. 

Goat meat is a significant source of protein for many families. 

The scheme promotes sustainable agricultural practices through livestock rearing. 

It encourages the use of local breeds which are better adapted to the environment. 

The establishment of goat units can also lead to increased production of goat milk. 

Goat milk is highly nutritious and can be a valuable addition to the diet. 

The scheme has the potential to enhance the overall economic condition of rural families. 

By diversifying income sources, farmers can reduce their dependency on traditional crops. 

The goat farming sector is also linked to various value-added products. 

These include goat leather and other by-products which can further increase income. 

The government has also initiated training programs for beneficiaries. 

These programs cover best practices in goat rearing and management. 

Training is essential for ensuring the success of the goat units. 

The scheme is part of a larger vision to boost the livestock sector in India. 

It aligns with the National Livestock Mission launched in 2014. 

The mission aims to enhance livestock production and productivity. 

It also focuses on improving the livelihoods of livestock farmers. 

The Establishment of Goat Unit (10 +1) scheme is an important component of this mission. 

It reflects the government's commitment to rural development and poverty alleviation. 

The scheme has been well-received by farmers across various states. 

It has shown promising results in states like Kerala and Tamil Nadu. 

These states have reported increased goat production and farmer incomes. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme's impact. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the program. 

The Establishment of Goat Unit (10 +1) scheme represents a significant step towards empowering rural communities. 

It provides a structured approach to livestock farming that can lead to sustainable development. 

Overall, the scheme is a vital initiative for enhancing rural livelihoods in India.
